newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO to allow non-members to decide standards.
newsitem.headline: NATO to allow non-members to decide standards.

text.p: NATO will allow its former cold-war enemies to take decisions affecting the standards of its military equipment, officials said on Friday.

After a meeting between NATO and countries taking part in the Partnership For Peace -- the alliance's programme to forge closer links with eastern Europe -- officials said they would cooperate on standards for equipment ranging from computer software to ammunition.
The decision was taken during the annual meeting of procurement chiefs from the 16-nation NATO and their counterparts from the 19 PFP states.
"It makes sense for everybody to cooperate on setting standards," a NATO official said. "It will make joint activities run more smoothly if everyone is operating from the same base."

Diplomats said it would also be a small step towards helping countries such as Poland -- which want PFP participation to be a stepping stone to NATO membership -- match the alliance's standards ahead of time.

Procurement chiefs are responsible for setting the standards on a wide range of NATO activities and equipment ranging from the manner in which ammunition is packed to the type of software used on its computers.
